note: Reviewed lifespans for the era record (data/hist-eras.js). `rows` act on the map (js/hist-scale.js eraSpanOut): the name is withheld in a year after `e` or before `s` (astronomical years; the bound year itself is inside). A row is written only where Wikidata states the bound AND the historical record agrees, and only if the bound withholds no year history says the polity existed: a row with `s` carries `hs`, the earliest year its `history` sentence places the unit, and the gate fails if the map withholds the name in any year from `hs` on. `refuted` are mechanical findings examined and NOT applied, with the reason. `facts` is what Wikidata states (P571/P576), refreshed by node scripts/histeras/spans.mjs --fetch. Gate: npm run check:histfidelity.

cadenceBasis.observed: estimate, not measured per class: Wikidata is edited continuously and its Query Service reflects an edit within minutes, so any day can change what a query answers
cadenceBasis.expires: if the builders read a Wikidata dump or a frozen snapshot instead of the live Query Service

rows.name: Songhai
rows.history: Battle of Tondibi (13 March 1591): the Saadian army defeated Askia Ishaq II and the empire broke up; the Dendi successor kingdom is a different unit.

rows.name: Watassid Morocco
rows.history: The Saadians took Fez in 1549; Ali Abu Hassun's Wattasid restoration ended at the Battle of Tadla, 1554.

rows.name: Inca Empire
rows.history: Cusco fell in 1533; the Neo-Inca state at Vilcabamba ended with the capture of Túpac Amaru in 1572 (the later of the two dates Wikidata states, so no year of Inca rule is withheld).

rows.name: Adal
rows.history: The Adal Sultanate ended in 1577, when its seat moved to Aussa and the Imamate of Aussa succeeded it.

rows.name: Wadai
rows.history: The Wadai Sultanate was founded by Abd al-Karim in 1635 (overthrowing the Tunjur).

rows.name: Vijayanagara
rows.history: Sriranga III, the last emperor, lost the last of his territory to Bijapur and Golconda by 1646.

rows.name: Bidar
rows.history: The Bidar Sultanate was annexed by Bijapur in 1619.

rows.name: Ahmadnagar
rows.history: Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah declared independence from the Bahmanis in 1490; the Mughals annexed the sultanate in 1636.

rows.name: Golkonda
rows.history: Quli Qutb Shah declared Golconda independent of the Bahmanis in 1518.

rows.name: Dutch Brazil
rows.history: The WIC took Olinda and Recife in 1630; the colony capitulated at Taborda in January 1654.

rows.name: New Amsterdam
rows.history: The shape is the Dutch colony of New Netherland around New Amsterdam: taken by the English in 1664 and ceded at Breda in 1667.

rows.name: Austrian Empire
rows.history: Francis II proclaimed the Austrian Empire on 11 August 1804; before that the Habsburg lands had no such name.

rows.name: Mali
rows.history: The Mali Empire broke up after the Bamana of Ségou sacked Niani, c. 1670.

rows.name: Dutch Republic
rows.history: The Act of Abjuration (1581) founded the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands.

rows.name: Tsardom of Muscovy
rows.history: Ivan IV was crowned the first Tsar on 16 January 1547; before that the state was the Grand Principality of Moscow.

rows.name: Sardinia-Piedmont
rows.history: Savoy received Sardinia, and the royal title, by the Treaty of The Hague (1720).

rows.name: Dutch Formosa
rows.history: Fort Zeelandia surrendered to Koxinga in February 1662.

rows.name: Nogai Horde
rows.history: The Great Nogai Horde disintegrated under Kalmyk pressure by 1634.

rows.name: Dutch East Indies
rows.history: The colony of that name was created when the VOC was dissolved and its possessions nationalised (1 January 1800).

rows.name: Hong Kong
rows.history: Hong Kong became a polity with British occupation in 1841; before that it was part of Xin'an County.

rows.name: Rozwi
rows.history: The Rozvi Empire arose under Changamire Dombo, c. 1660 (later accounts: 1684), so no year it existed is withheld.

rows.name: Pegu
rows.history: The Hanthawaddy kingdom («Pegu») was absorbed by Toungoo, whose conquest of Lower Burma was complete by 1552; the Restored Hanthawaddy (1740) is a separate unit.

rows.name: Astrakhan Khanate
rows.history: Muscovy annexed the Astrakhan Khanate in 1556.

rows.name: Mughal Empire
rows.history: Babur founded the empire at the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

rows.name: Alwa
rows.history: Soba, the capital of Alodia, fell to the Funj c. 1504.

rows.name: Khanate of Sibir
rows.history: The Siberian Khanate formed under the Taibugids c. 1490.

rows.name: Berar
rows.history: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk declared Berar independent of the Bahmanis in 1490.

rows.name: Papua New Guinea
rows.history: The name names only the state that became independent in 1975; no polity of that name existed earlier.

rows.name: Kalmar Union
rows.history: Erik of Pomerania was crowned at Kalmar in 1397; Sweden left the union in 1523.

rows.name: Denmark-Norway
rows.history: The realm called Denmark-Norway dates from 1536-37, when Norway's council was abolished after Sweden left the Kalmar Union (1523); it did not exist in 1000.

rows.name: Timurid Empire
rows.history: Timur took power at Balkh in 1370.

rows.name: Khmer Empire
rows.history: Ayutthaya sacked Angkor in 1431.

rows.name: Beylik of Aydin
rows.history: The Ottomans annexed the Aydınid beylik in 1426.

rows.name: Nanzan
rows.history: Shō Hashi conquered Nanzan in 1429 and unified Ryukyu.

rows.name: Chūzan
rows.history: Chūzan became the unified Ryukyu Kingdom in 1429.

rows.name: Hokuzan
rows.history: Chūzan conquered Hokuzan in 1416.

rows.name: Ilkhanate
rows.history: Hülegü's campaign established the Ilkhanate in 1256; it disintegrated on the death of Abu Sa'id (1335).

rows.name: Mamluke Sultanate
rows.history: The Mamluks seized power in Egypt in 1250.

rows.name: Seljuk Caliphate
rows.history: The Sultanate of Rum ended with the death of Mesud II, 1307-08.

rows.name: Srivijaya Empire
rows.history: Majapahit conquered Palembang in 1377, ending Srivijaya.

rows.name: Kediri
rows.history: Ken Arok defeated Kertajaya of Kediri at Ganter (1222 in most accounts); every year the sheets draw it in (from 1240) is after both dates.

rows.name: Pagan
rows.history: The Pagan kingdom fell after the Mongol invasions; Kyawswa was deposed in 1297.

rows.name: Chola state
rows.history: Rajendra III, the last Chola king, was defeated by the Pandyas c. 1279.

rows.name: Shogun Japan (Kamakura)
rows.history: The Kamakura shogunate fell with the siege of Kamakura (July 1333).

rows.name: Sukhothai
rows.history: Sukhothai was founded in 1238 and annexed by Ayutthaya in 1438.

rows.name: Kingdom of Sukhotai
rows.history: As «Sukhothai».

rows.name: Chimú
rows.history: The Inca conquered Chimor c. 1470.

rows.name: Bulgar Khanate
rows.history: At 1279-1400 the shape is the Second Bulgarian Empire, which fell to the Ottomans (Tarnovo 1393, Vidin 1396).

rows.name: Ghaznavid Emirate
rows.history: Alp Tigin took Ghazni in 962; the Ghurids took Lahore, the last Ghaznavid seat, in 1186-87.

rows.name: Buwayhid Emirates
rows.history: The Buyid dynasty ruled from 934 until the Seljuks ended it in 1062.

rows.name: Buyiids
rows.history: As «Buwayhid Emirates».

rows.name: Liao
rows.history: The Liao dynasty was proclaimed in 916 and fell to the Jin in 1125.

rows.name: Dutchy of Benevento
rows.history: The Lombard principality of Benevento ended with the Norman conquest (1077) and the city passed to the Papacy (1081).

rows.name: Tiahuanaco Empire
rows.history: The Tiwanaku polity collapsed c. 1000-1150.

rows.name: Fatimid Caliphate
rows.history: Saladin abolished the Fatimid Caliphate in 1171.

rows.name: Almoravid dynasty
rows.history: The Almohads took Marrakesh in 1147.

rows.name: Kakheti-Hereti
rows.history: David IV annexed Kakheti-Hereti in 1104.

rows.name: Principality of Galicia-Volhynia
rows.history: Roman Mstislavich united Galicia and Volhynia in 1199.

rows.name: Principality of Novgorod
rows.history: Novgorod expelled its prince in 1136 and became a republic.

rows.name: Mongol Empire
rows.history: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan at the kurultai of 1206.

rows.name: Kamarupa
rows.history: The Pala dynasty of Kamarupa ended c. 1140.

rows.name: Angevin Empire
rows.history: Henry II became King of England in 1154.

rows.name: Kingdom of Georgia
rows.history: Bagrat III united Abkhazia and Kartli as the Kingdom of Georgia in 1008.

rows.name: Holy Roman Empire
rows.history: Otto I was crowned emperor in 962.

rows.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
rows.history: The Caliphate of Córdoba was abolished in 1031.

rows.name: Khazars
rows.history: The Khazar khaganate emerged c. 618-650 and was broken by Sviatoslav in 965-69; the later of Wikidata's dates (1048) is kept so no year is over-withheld.

rows.name: Kingdom of France
rows.history: The Kingdom of France is dated from the election of Hugh Capet (987); before that the realm is West Francia.

rows.name: Poland
rows.history: The Polish state is dated from Mieszko I, c. 960 (baptism 966).

rows.name: Pratiharas
rows.history: The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty ended c. 1036.

rows.name: Nan Chao
rows.history: Nanzhao fell in 902; the Dali Kingdom (937) is a separate unit.

rows.name: Wessex
rows.history: Æthelstan became King of the English in 927.

rows.name: Silla
rows.history: Gyeongsun of Silla surrendered to Goryeo in 935.

rows.name: Great Moravia
rows.history: Great Moravia collapsed under the Magyars, c. 907.

rows.name: Balhae
rows.history: The Khitans destroyed Balhae in 926.

rows.name: Saffarids
rows.history: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth took power in Sistan in 861.

rows.name: Kyivan Rus
rows.history: Oleg took Kyiv in 882.

rows.name: Carolingian Empire
rows.history: Charlemagne was crowned emperor in 800; the empire split after the deposition of Charles the Fat (887).

rows.name: Papal States
rows.history: The Donation of Pepin (754-56) founded the Papal States.

rows.name: Emirate of Córdoba
rows.history: Abd al-Rahman I founded the emirate in 756; Abd al-Rahman III proclaimed the caliphate in 929.

rows.name: Tibetan Empire
rows.history: The Tibetan Empire fragmented after the death of Langdarma (842).

rows.name: Tang Empire
rows.history: The Tang dynasty ruled 618-907.

rows.name: Aghlabid Emirate
rows.history: Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab was made emir in 800; the Fatimids took Raqqada in 909.

rows.name: Pallava
rows.history: The Pallava dynasty ended when the Cholas defeated Aparajita, c. 897.

rows.name: Essex
rows.history: Essex submitted to Wessex in 825.

rows.name: Kent
rows.history: Kent passed to Wessex in 825 and was a West Saxon sub-kingdom until 871.

rows.name: Barghawata
rows.history: The Barghawata confederacy was founded in 744.

rows.name: Paekche
rows.history: Tang and Silla conquered Baekje in 660.

rows.name: Koguryo
rows.history: Goguryeo is traditionally founded in 37 BCE and fell to Tang and Silla in 668.

rows.name: Sasanian Empire
rows.history: Yazdegerd III, the last Sasanian, died in 651.

rows.name: Sui Empire
rows.history: The Sui dynasty ruled 581-618.

rows.name: Göktürks
rows.history: Bumin Qaghan founded the Turkic Khaganate in 552.

rows.name: Western Roman Empire
rows.history: Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus in 476.

rows.name: Jin Empire
rows.history: The Eastern Jin ended in 420 (Liu Song).

rows.name: Northern Liang
rows.history: Northern Liang ruled 397-439.

rows.name: Han Zhao
rows.history: Han Zhao ruled 304-329.

rows.name: Gupta Empire
rows.history: The Gupta Empire is dated from Chandragupta I, c. 320.

rows.name: Jin
rows.history: Sima Yan founded the Jin dynasty in 266.

rows.name: Parthian Empire
rows.history: Ardashir I defeated Artabanus IV at Hormozgan in 224.

rows.name: Han
rows.history: The Han dynasty ended with the abdication of Emperor Xian in 220.

rows.name: Satavahanihara
rows.history: The Satavahana dynasty ended c. 220-224.

rows.name: Suren Kingdom
rows.history: The Indo-Parthian kingdom of the Suren house ended c. 226.

rows.name: Dacia
rows.history: Trajan conquered Dacia in 106.

rows.name: Nabatean Kingdom
rows.history: Rome annexed Nabataea in 106.

rows.name: Odrysian Kingdom
rows.history: Thrace became a Roman province in 46.

rows.name: Kushan Empire
rows.history: Kujula Kadphises founded the Kushan Empire, c. 30.

rows.name: Seleucid Kingdom
rows.history: Pompey annexed the Seleucid remnant in 63 BCE.

rows.name: Mauryan Empire
rows.history: Pushyamitra Shunga overthrew the last Maurya in 185 BCE.

rows.name: Nan-Yue
rows.history: Zhao Tuo established Nanyue in 207-204 BCE (the earlier of the two Wikidata dates is kept); the Han conquered it in 111 BCE.

rows.name: Min-Yue
rows.history: The Han conquered Minyue in 110 BCE.

rows.name: Han Empire
rows.history: The Han dynasty is dated from 206 BCE.

rows.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
rows.history: Ptolemy I took the royal title in 305 BCE.

rows.name: Atropatene
rows.history: Atropates made Media Atropatene independent after Alexander's death (323 BCE).

rows.name: Xiongnu
rows.history: The Xiongnu first appear in the record in 318 BCE (and as a confederation under Modu, 209 BCE); every year the sheet draws them in precedes both.

rows.name: Achaemenid Empire
rows.history: Cyrus II overthrew Astyages in 550 BCE.

rows.name: Assyria
rows.history: The Neo-Assyrian Empire ended at Harran, 609 BCE.

rows.name: Urartu
rows.history: The Kingdom of Urartu is attested from Aramu, c. 860 BCE.

refuted.name: Songhai
refuted.note: Before 1464 the Songhai state of Gao (Sonni dynasty) already existed; 1464 is the start of the imperial expansion under Sonni Ali.

refuted.name: Bidar
refuted.note: Barid Shahi rule at Bidar began in 1492; 1527 is the end of nominal Bahmani suzerainty.

refuted.name: Mali
refuted.note: A kingdom of Mali (Malal) is attested from the 11th century (al-Bakri, 1068); 1235 is the founding of the empire.

refuted.name: Bulgar Khanate
refuted.note: On the 1000 and 1100 sheets upstream uses the same name for the First Bulgarian Empire (681-1018); one name, two units — unresolved, see dev-notes/2026-10-01-hist-era-span-fidelity.md.

refuted.name: Suren Kingdom
refuted.note: Gondophares' accession is dated variously from c. 20 BCE to c. 20 CE.

refuted.name: Ur
refuted.note: Ur was occupied from the Ubaid period (5th millennium BCE); Wikidata's 3800 BCE is later than the archaeological record.

refuted.name: Hittites
refuted.note: Wikidata states an inception of +1500 CE for the Hittites — evidently an error (the Hittite kingdom is dated c. 1650-1180 BCE). Not applied; reported upstream-side in the dev note.

refuted.name: Saba
refuted.note: Saba is dated from the 12th to the 8th century BCE depending on the source; the record does not fix 1000 BCE.

refuted.name: Wu
refuted.note: Wu is traditionally founded by Taibo (12th-11th c. BCE); 900 BCE is not a date history fixes.

refuted.name: Gandhāra
refuted.note: Gandhara names the region, which outlived the Achaemenid conquest (c. 535 BCE).

refuted.name: Kosala
refuted.note: Kosala's annexation by Magadha is dated only to the 5th century BCE.

refuted.name: Magadha
refuted.note: Magadha names the realm of successive dynasties (Nanda, Maurya, Gupta), not only the kingdom Wikidata ends in 345 BCE.

refuted.name: New Zealand
refuted.note: A geographic name for the islands.

refuted.name: Iceland
refuted.note: A geographic name for the island.

refuted.name: Kadambas
refuted.note: The Kadambas of Banavasi ended c. 540, later than Wikidata's 525.

refuted.name: Alwa
refuted.note: Alodia is attested in the 6th century (conversion, c. 580); Wikidata's 600 is later.

refuted.name: Göktürks
refuted.note: The Second Turkic Khaganate (682-744) is also Göktürk; the 657 end is the Western Khaganate's.

refuted.name: Huari Empire
refuted.note: Wari is dated from c. 500-600; Wikidata's 600 is the later bound.

refuted.name: Huari Empire
refuted.note: Wari collapsed c. 1000; Wikidata's 1100 is generous but not stated by the record. Left as drawn.

refuted.name: Dvaravati
refuted.note: Dvaravati is dated from the 6th century.

refuted.name: Nobatia
refuted.note: Nobatia merged with Makuria at some point before 707; 650 is not fixed.

refuted.name: Chen-La
refuted.note: Chenla continued, divided into Land and Water Chenla, until the Khmer Empire (802).

refuted.name: Visigothic Kingdom
refuted.note: The last Visigothic king Ardo held Septimania until c. 721; Wikidata's 718 is earlier.

refuted.name: Ghana
refuted.note: The upstream draws the Ghana Empire, not the Republic of Ghana (1957).

refuted.name: Gurjara Pratihara
refuted.note: The Gurjara-Pratiharas are dated from Nagabhata I, c. 730.

refuted.name: Sindh
refuted.note: The upstream draws Sindh under the Habbari emirate, not the British division (1843).

refuted.name: Kingdom of Norway
refuted.note: Harald Fairhair's unification is dated c. 872; Wikidata's 900 is later.

refuted.name: Pechenegs
refuted.note: A people, not a dated polity.

refuted.name: Madagascar
refuted.note: A geographic name for the island.

refuted.name: Tibet
refuted.note: The upstream draws Tibet as a region and its successive states, not the 1912-1951 state.

refuted.name: Yemen
refuted.note: A geographic name for the region.

refuted.name: Georgia
refuted.note: A geographic name; the polity is drawn separately as «Kingdom of Georgia».

refuted.name: Croatia
refuted.note: The upstream draws the medieval Kingdom of Croatia (925), not the republic (1991).

refuted.name: Toltec Empire
refuted.note: Tula fell c. 1150-1179; Wikidata's 1122 is earlier.

refuted.name: Nepal
refuted.note: The upstream draws the Kathmandu valley kingdoms, not the Gorkha state (1768).

refuted.name: Bhutan
refuted.note: A geographic name for the region.

refuted.name: Benin
refuted.note: The upstream draws the Kingdom of Benin, not the Republic of Benin (1960).

refuted.name: Great Khanate
refuted.note: The Great Khan's realm predates the Yuan proclamation (1271).

refuted.name: Great Khanate
refuted.note: The Northern Yuan continued the Great Khanate after 1368.

refuted.name: Aymara kingdoms
refuted.note: The Inca conquest of the Aymara kingdoms is dated variously (c. 1438-1470s).

refuted.name: Moldova
refuted.note: The upstream draws the Principality of Moldavia (1346), not the republic (1991).

refuted.name: Blue Horde
refuted.note: The White/Blue Horde naming is contested and no source fixes its end at 1395.

refuted.name: Philippines
refuted.note: A geographic name for the archipelago.

refuted.name: Cambodia
refuted.note: A geographic name (Kambuja), not the 1953 kingdom.

refuted.name: Funj
refuted.note: The Funj are a people attested before the Sennar sultanate (1504); the name does not claim the sultanate.

refuted.name: Laos
refuted.note: The upstream draws Lan Xang, not the 1949 state.

refuted.name: Otavalo
refuted.note: The upstream draws the Otavalo people, not the city (1534).

refuted.name: Calvas
refuted.note: The upstream draws the Calvas people, not the canton (1824).

refuted.name: Natchez
refuted.note: The upstream draws the Natchez people, not the settlement (1716).

refuted.name: White Horde
refuted.note: The White/Blue Horde naming is contested and no source fixes its end at 1500.

refuted.name: Oman
refuted.note: A geographic name for the region.

refuted.name: Senegal
refuted.note: A geographic name for the region.

refuted.name: Shan states
refuted.note: The Shan states persisted under Burmese suzerainty until 1885 and as British protectorates until 1948; Wikidata's 1563 is not their end.

refuted.name: Republic of the Seven Zenden
refuted.note: The Zenden of the Valais governed themselves from the 15th century; 1613 is a formal date.

refuted.name: Belize
refuted.note: A place name in use since the 17th century.

refuted.name: Surinam
refuted.note: The English colony of Surinam (1650-1667) is a different unit from the Dutch colony (1667).

refuted.name: Cayenne
refuted.note: The upstream draws French Guiana, not the town founded in 1664.

refuted.name: Ceylon
refuted.note: A geographic name for the island, not British Ceylon (1815).

refuted.name: Khanate of the Golden Horde
refuted.note: Batu established the Golden Horde on his return from the western campaign, 1242-43 (and the Ulus of Jochi it continued existed from the 1220s); Wikidata's 1243 would withhold the name in 1242.

refuted.name: Elam
refuted.note: Wikidata's 2700 BCE is the start of the Old Elamite period; the historical record dates Elamite civilization from the Proto-Elamite period, c. 3200 BCE (Susa and Anshan, the Proto-Elamite script), so the bound would withhold the name from the 3000 BCE sheet in years Elam existed (the row did so from 2026-10-01 until this verdict).

Q210551.en: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
